main_body: Japanese-style townhouse seen from the front: a large grey-blue tile roof, a cream plaster band, a small lower eave, then a lattice wooden ground floor with an open dark doorway and straw bundles
top_band: Roof: a light grey ridge cap on rows 1-6, then a tiled slope of mid and dark blue-grey on rows 7-30, with a dark edge on rows 30-31
evidence: Down a middle column I read a light ridge cap (rows 1-6) and a tall tiled roof slope (rows 7-30). The slope ends in a dark edge on rows 30-31 that reads as the front edge and eave shadow. Below it come the plaster wall, a second small roof (rows 41-47) and the wooden lattice storey. The roof slope is a large visible top surface like the Beodeul house roofs, and it sits well above the vertical walls. The dark doorway is inset between the lattice panels. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 blue-grey steps with per-tile highlights and dark gaps, comparable to the reference tile roofs. The wooden wall has slat grain and dark slits, and the straw bundles are shaded in several yellows. Outlines are dark navy or dark brown tinted to the adjacent material, not pure black. The cream plaster band is the flattest area, with only a few tone variations and no speckle, so it is slightly plainer than the reference plaster. Overall richness is close to the reference.
